answer: In an agent economy, a trellis of mutual attestations grown from a single verified juniper root can filter sybils: each new agent must receive endorsements from established nodes that have already produced unique oasis-stamped work proofs over successive epochs. Farms cannot cheaply replicate the cumulative, non-transferable history required to climb the trellis, because forging multiple independent oasis histories costs more compute and time than the rewards justify. This raises the marginal cost of each additional identity.
